rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: The verse covers three recurrent cases: the financially incompetent spendthrift, the mentally deficient, and one unable to dictate because absent or ill; their guardians are respectively a guardian or executor, father or executor, and agent, with the mute among the weak or unable.
rows.anchor: ذكر تعالى ثلاثة أنواع تقع نوازلهم في كل زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasizing “he himself” removes a possible figurative reading and specifies that the debtor cannot dictate personally.
rows.anchor: وفيه من الفصاحة ما لا يخفى، لأن في التأكيد به رفع المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rare reading quiesces the hāʾ of huwa after a word ending in a vowel, treating a separated form like a connected one; this is more exceptional than a reading after thumma.
rows.anchor: وقرىء شاذا بإسكان هاء: هو، وإن كان قد سبقها ما ينفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “his guardian” refers to the debtor, one of the three vulnerable cases; al-Zamakhsharī identifies an executor, agent, or interpreter who dictates with the debtor's approval.
rows.anchor: الضمير في وليه عائد على أحد هؤلاء الثلاثة، وهو الذي عليه الحق

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the pronoun to refer to the debt, making the guardian the creditor; this is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Rabīʿ.
rows.anchor: وذهب الطبري إلى أن الضمير في وليه يعود على الحق، فيكون الولي

rows.speaker: ابن عطية، الراغب
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects attributing the creditor-as-guardian view to Ibn ʿAbbās because a creditor's dictation cannot establish a debt against a spendthrift; al-Rāghib likewise says a claimant's assertion has no force.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ولا يصح عن ابن عباس، وكيف تشهد البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in “with justice” may attach to the dictation verb or mark its state or manner.
rows.anchor: و: بالعدل، متعلق بقوله: فليملل، ويحتمل أن تكون الباء للحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With justice” urges fairness toward both creditor and ward; the verse supports legal interdiction of a minor and transactions by a spendthrift under guardianship.
rows.anchor: بالعدل، حث على تحريه لصاحب الحق، والمولى عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Seek two witnesses” is a request for testimony or equivalent to “make two witnesses”; shahīd is intensive, suggesting experienced witnesses whose repeated use indicates acceptance and integrity.
rows.anchor: واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم أي: اطلبوا للإشهاد شهيدين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing believers as “your men” indicates non-Muslims are not witnesses here; the verse does not address testimony among non-Muslims, which Abū Ḥanīfa allows even across religions. It also indicates adult male witnesses.
rows.anchor: من رجالكم، الخطاب للمؤمنين، وهم المصدر بهم الآية،

rows.speaker: شريح، ابن سيرين، ابن شبرمة، عثمان البتي
rows.claim: They accept a slave's testimony; reports also attribute acceptance to ʿAlī, with Ibrāhīm permitting testimony in trivial matters and Anas saying he knows no one who rejected it.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية أنه: يجوز شهادة العبد، وهو مذهب شريح،

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority, including leading Ḥanafīs, Mālik, and al-Shāfiʿī, reject slave testimony in all matters; this is also narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Ḥasan.
rows.anchor:
وقال الجمهور:
أبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف، ومحمد، وزفر،

rows.speaker: الثوري، أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، ابن شبرمة، الشافعي
rows.claim: They say children's testimony is not considered; Ibn Abī Laylā permits children's mutual testimony, and Mālik permits it in injuries under conditions.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية يدل على أن شهادة الصبيان لا تعتبر، وبه قال الثوري،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent requirement is simply that the two principal witnesses be men; jurists disagree over testimony by a blind witness.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية اشتراط الرجولية فقط في الشاهدين.

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة، محمد
rows.claim: They categorically reject testimony by a blind witness; the same view is narrated from ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr, and Iyās b. Muʿāwiya.
rows.anchor: ذهب أبو حنيفة، ومحمد إلى أنه لا يجوز بحال.

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى، أبو يوسف، الشافعي، زفر، شريح، الشعبي، مالك، الليث
rows.claim: They differ: Ibn Abī Laylā, Abū Yūsuf, and al-Shāfiʿī accept testimony learned before blindness; Zufar permits only lineage; Shurayḥ and al-Shaʿbī accept it generally; Mālik and al-Layth rely on voice recognition in some matters but reject testimony in adultery or false accusation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي ليلى، وأبو يوسف، والشافعي: إذا علم قبل العمى جازت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some accept a mute witness through gestures and some reject the testimony; deaf witnesses are rejected for spoken claims but accepted for other sensory matters.
rows.anchor: ولو كان الشاهد أخرس، فقيل: تقبل شهادته بإشارة، وسواء كان طارئا أم أصليا،

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Reports from Mālik restrict a Bedouin's testimony against a settled person to injuries, with another report allowing specified travel-related testament and sale cases.
rows.anchor: ولو شهد بدوي على قروي، فروى ابن وهب عن مالك أنها لا تجوز إلا في الجراح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If the two are not men” may mean the creditor failed or chose not to obtain two men; another view requires that two men be unavailable before two women may be called.
rows.anchor: فإن لم يكونا رجلين الضمير عائد على الشهيدين أي: فإن لم يكن الشهيدان رجلين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “One man and two women” admits several ellipses and parses: an omitted witness, a subject with omitted predicate, or a man as subject or passive object of an implied verb.
rows.anchor: فرجل وامرأتان ارتفاع رجل على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي: فلشاهد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nonstandard reading quiesces the hamza in wa-imraʾatān, perhaps easing successive vowels; a poetic line illustrates the sound change.
rows.anchor: وقرىء شاذا: وامرأتان، بهمزة ساكنة، وهو على غير قياس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording permits one man's and two women's testimony in all debt contracts, including consideration, marriage, benefits, and intentional blood claims; excluding a contract requires evidence.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية يقتضي جواز شهادة المرأتين مع الرجل في سائر عقود المداينات،

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī rejects women's testimony with men outside property matters; for wills he accepts men for nonfinancial dispositions and women for financial dispositions.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: لا تجوز شهادة النساء مع الرجال في غير الأموال،

rows.speaker: الليث، الأوزاعي، الحسن بن حيي، الثوري، مالك
rows.claim: Their positions differ on wills, emancipation, marriage, divorce, penalties, retaliation, agency, and lineage: al-Layth allows wills and emancipation; al-Awzāʿī bars marriage; al-Ḥasan b. Ḥayy bars penalties; al-Thawrī bars only penalties; Mālik excludes penalties and personal-status matters.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: تجوز شهادة النساء في الوصية والعتق، ولا تجوز في النكاح

rows.speaker: الحسن، الضحاك؛ عمر، عطاء، الشعبي؛ شريح؛ عمر وابنه عبد الله؛ علي
rows.claim: Other reported views limit women to debt, allow divorce, allow emancipation, allow one man with two women in marriage, or allow testimony in a contract, respectively.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن، والضحاك: لا تجوز شهادتهن إلا في الدين.

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، محمد، زفر، عثمان البتي
rows.claim: They reject women's testimony with men in penalties and retaliation but accept it for other rights.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف، ومحمد، وزفر، وعثمان البتي: لا تقبل شهادة النساء مع الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no disagreement that women may testify alone about childbirth, virginity, a newborn's first cry, women's defects, and comparable matters specific to women.
rows.anchor: وأما قبول شهادتهن مفردات فلا خلاف في قبولها في: الولادة،

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa accepts one upright woman's testimony for moon sighting as information, and also accepts a midwife alone.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو حنيفة شهادة الواحدة العادلة في رؤية الهلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among witnesses whom you approve” most likely modifies “seek witnesses,” applying approval to all combinations; adjective and substitution analyses are weak.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه متعلق بقوله: واستشهدوا، أي: واستشهدوا ممن ترضون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in “you approve” is apparently to believers, implying that witnesses are not presumed upright by status alone; other views address judges or creditors.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في ترضون ظاهره أنه للمؤمنين،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الشعبي، الحسن، النخعي، الخصاف
rows.claim: They define approved witnesses as people of merit, religion, and competence; untainted in sex or lineage; not known for misconduct or suspicion; or with good deeds outweighing bad deeds while avoiding major sins.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: من أهل الفضل والدين والكفاءة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view requires ten traits: freedom, adulthood, Islam, integrity, knowledge, no personal gain or self-protection, no habitual error, preserved social decency, and no enmity toward the accused.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المرضي من الشهود من اجتمعت فيه عشر خصال:

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abū Yūsuf accepts a person whose good conduct outweighs minor sins and who avoids major offenses; he excludes gamblers, habitual prayer neglecters, notorious liars, and those who insult the Companions or neighbors, among other conduct.
rows.anchor: وذكر بشر بن الوليد عن أبي يوسف: أن من سلم من الفواحش

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى، أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، محمد
rows.claim: They accept upright witnesses from sectarian groups except the Khaṭṭābiyya among the Rāfiḍa; Muḥammad rejects Kharijites but accepts Ḥarūriyya because he distinguishes their treatment of Muslims' property.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي ليلى، وأبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف: تقبل شهادة أهل الأهواء العدول،

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة، إياس بن معاوية، بلال بن أبي بردة، عمر بن عبد العزيز، شريح، أبو هريرة، محمد
rows.claim: Reports reject witnesses for miserliness, sea-trading, eating clay, plucking or hiding the beard, answering a disparaging nickname, slave dealing, frivolity, effeminacy, or flying pigeons; Shurayḥ's anecdote illustrates the nickname ruling.
rows.anchor: وعن إياس بن معاوية لا يجيز شهادة الأشراف بالعراق ولا البخلاء،

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى، مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Laylā rejects a poor witness because poverty may prompt desire for money; Mālik rejects beggars in substantial matters but accepts testimony in trivial ones.
rows.anchor: ابن أبي ليلى شهادة الفقير، وقال: لا يؤمن أن يحمله فقره

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: One report rejects a witness whose usual conduct is sinful or indecent; another accepts one whose usual conduct is obedience and who has committed no major sin.
rows.anchor: وعن الشافعي: إذا كان الأغلب من حاله المعصية وعدم المروءة ردت شهادته،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muruwwa means restraint, dignified bearing, respect for social obligations, and avoiding vulgarity and frivolity, not fine clothing, mounts, tools, or appearance.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن تفسر المروءة بالتصاون، والسمت الحسن، وحفظ الحرمة،

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: In his letter to Abū Mūsā, ʿUmar says Muslims are upright for one another unless punished, known for false testimony, suspect, or disqualified by kinship.
rows.anchor: ففي كتاب عمر لأبي موسى: والمسلمون عدول بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: الحسن، ابن شبرمة، محمد، أبو يوسف، مالك، الليث، الشافعي
rows.claim: They differ over investigating witnesses: al-Ḥasan accepts unless impeached; Ibn Shubrumah investigates if challenged; Muḥammad and Abū Yūsuf always investigate; Mālik requires private inquiry; al-Layth lets the opponent produce discrediting evidence; al-Shāfiʿī adds public attestation after private clearance.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد، وأبو يوسف: يسأل عنهم، وإن لم يطعن فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Regional jurists agree testimony for a child or parent is invalid, apart from reported exceptions; the dominant view bars either spouse testifying for the other.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ذكر من اعتبار نفي التهمة عن الشاهد إذا كان عدلا، فاتفق

rows.speaker: البتي، إياس بن معاوية
rows.claim: Al-Battī permits a child for parents and a father for child and wife; Iyās is reported to permit testimony for one's son.
rows.anchor: إلا ما حكي عن البتي، قال: تجوز شهادة الولد لوالديه،

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، محمد، زفر، مالك، الأوزاعي، الليث
rows.claim: They reject testimony by either spouse for the other; employee testimony is also disputed, with Mālik requiring notable integrity, al-Awzāʿī rejecting it, and al-Thawrī allowing it absent personal benefit.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف، ومحمد، وزفر، ومالك، والأوزاعي، والليث إلى أنه: لا يجوز

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، مالك
rows.claim: The Ḥanafīs do not readmit testimony rejected for sinfulness or marriage but accept after rejection for slavery, unbelief, or childhood; Mālik also bars readmission after slavery or childhood.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة، وأصحابه: لا تقبل إذا ردت لفسق أو زوجية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent rules require two men or one man and two women, and thus do not allow judgment on one witness plus an oath; the Ḥanafīs and others agree.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية: أن الشهود في الديون رجلان، أو رجل وامرأتان،

rows.speaker: مالك، الشافعي، أحمد، إسحاق، أبو عبيد
rows.claim: They permit one witness plus an oath in financial claims, citing the four caliphs and Medinan practice; reports from al-Zuhrī differ on whether this was innovation and when it began.
rows.anchor:
وقال مالك، والشافعي وأتباعهما، وأحمد، وإسحاق، وأبو عبيد:
يحكم به في الأموال خاصة،

rows.speaker: الأعمش، حمزة
rows.claim: They read in tadhilla with a kasra as a conditional particle and fa-tudhakkiru with doubled dhāl and a jussive response.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعمش، وحمزة: إن تضل بكسر الهمزة، جعلها حرف شرط.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers use subjunctive an and coordinate fa-tudhakkira; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr lighten the kāf, while others double it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح همزة: أن، وهي الناصبة، وفتح راء فتذكر

rows.speaker: الجحدري، عيسى بن عمران، حميد بن عبد الرحمن، مجاهد، زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Variants include passive tadhalla “be forgotten,” a form meaning testimony goes astray, fa-tudhakkiru “then she reminds,” and reciprocal fa-tadhākara.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وعيسى بن عمران: تضل، بضم التاء وفتح الضاد مبنيا للمفعول،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the conditional reading, the clause may describe the two women as an adjective, though its placement after the earlier descriptor raises a syntactic concern.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: في موضع رفع بكونه صفة للمذكر، وهما المرأتان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With open an, the clause is a purpose-cause: the possibility of forgetting is expressed as the reason for the other to remind, carried by meaning like preparing a prop for a wall that may lean.
rows.anchor: وأما: أن تضل، بفتح الهمزة، فهو في موضع المفعول من أجله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetfulness means failing to find one's way in testimony through forgetting or inattention, answered by reminding.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الضلال هنا هو عدم الاهتداء للشهادة لنسيان أو غفلة، ولذلك قوبل بقوله: فتذكر،

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء، سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: They explain the light reading as making the two women's combined testimony equivalent to a man's; al-Zamakhsharī calls this aberrant and Ibn ʿAṭiyya distant and wrong.
rows.anchor: وأما ما روي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء، وسفيان بن عيينة من أن قراءة التخفيف، فتذكر، معناه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He agrees with al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya: the reading fails linguistically because the verb is not recorded with that causative sense, and logically because both women's testimony, not one woman's reminder, would make the equivalent.
rows.anchor: وما قالاه صحيح، وينبو عنه اللفظ من جهة اللغة ومن جهة المعنى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either woman may forget and either may remind, so “one of them” is generic; the ordinary parse makes the other woman the one reminded, though object-first order is possible.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: إن ضلت هذه أذكرتها هذه، وإن ضلت هذه أذكرتها هذه،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An interpretation links women's forgetfulness to cold and moisture, says one woman's forgetting is more likely than both forgetting, and infers men's superiority.
rows.anchor: أن النسيان غالب على طباع النساء لكثرة البرد والرطوبة،

rows.speaker: النحاس عن علي بن سليمان عن أبي العباس
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās analyzes it as “for fear that one forget”; Abū Jaʿfar rejects this because it would make the purpose that the other woman remind her.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: سمعت علي بن سليمان يحكي عن أبي العباس أن التقدير:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tudhakkiru takes an omitted object, “the testimony”; the wording implies a witness must remember testimony and cannot rely only on writing, supported by 43:86.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى دلالة على أن من شرط جواز إقامة الشهادة ذكر الشاهد لها،

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، الشافعي، ابن أبي ليلى، الثوري
rows.claim: The first three require recollection beyond handwriting; Ibn Abī Laylā allows recognition of the handwriting, and al-Thawrī allows testimony if the witness recalls witnessing but not the amount.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف، والشافعي: إذا كتب خطه بالشهادة فلا يشهد حتى يذكرها،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda relates an occasion of revelation in which a man passed through a large gathering at Ḥirāʾ and no one accompanied him.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: سبب نزولها أن الرجل كان يطوف في الحراء العظيم،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الربيع؛ عطاء، الحسن؛ الشعبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Rabīʿ read the summons as initial bearing; ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḥasan consider it advisory, while al-Shaʿbī requires it when no other witness exists.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، وقتادة، والربيع وغيرهم.

rows.speaker: مجاهد، عطاء، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، الضحاك، السدي، إبراهيم، ابن زيد، النقاش
rows.claim: They read the summons as performing testimony already witnessed; al-Naqqāsh attributes this to the Prophet and says, if authentic, it makes the prohibition binding.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى: ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا لأداء الشهادة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya combines both readings: assistance is recommended when witnesses are plentiful, nearly obligatory in necessity, and obligatory if delay would destroy the right, especially when summoned to perform testimony already borne.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والآية كما قال الحسن، جمعت الأمرين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recording every debt and due date protects property and prevents disputes; “small” comes first to stress that minor debts matter, and the due date is the parties' agreed term.
rows.anchor: نهى أيضا عن السآمة في كتابة الدين، كل ذلك ضبط لأموال الناس، وتحريض على أن لا يقع النزاع،

rows.speaker: الماتريدي، author
rows.claim: Al-Māturīdī infers advance sale of clothing from “small or large”; Abū Ḥayyān objects that these words mean little or much, including amounts of grain.
rows.anchor: وقال الماتريدي: فيه دلالة على جواز السلم في الثياب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Become weary” is explained as “be lazy” or “be annoyed”; grammarians debate whether saʾima takes its object directly or through a preposition. A hadith and 4:142 are parallels for laziness.
rows.anchor: قيل: ومعنى: ولا تسأموا، أي لا تكسلوا، وعبر بالسأم عن الكسل،

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd's line about tiring of life witnesses the construction saʾima min.
rows.anchor: ولقد سئمت من الحياة وطولها ... وسؤال هذا الناس كيف لبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “write it” refers to the earlier debt or nearby right, equivalent in sense; those with many debts might tire of documentation.
rows.anchor: وضمير النصب في: تكتبوه، عائد على الدين، لسبقه، أو على الحق لقربه،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests the pronoun means the document, which may be concise or detailed without being deficient; Abū Ḥayyān calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير للكتاب،

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī reads “they should not tire” and “they should write”; the plural likely refers to witnesses, but may shift to parties or scribes.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: ولا يسأموا، بالياء وكذلك: أن يكتبوه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Small or large” is a state of the debt being written; supplying omitted kāna is misplaced. “Until its due date” means the debt remains established in liability until maturity, not that writing lasts the entire term.
rows.anchor: والتقدير: أن تكتبوه مستقرا في الذمة إلى أجل حلوله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is more just” points either to writing alone or to writing, testimony, and all prior means of documentation; aqsaṭ means more equitable, though its derivation is debated.
rows.anchor: ذلكم أقسط عند الله الإشارة إلى أقرب مذكور وهو الكتابة، وقيل الكتابة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري، ابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives aqsaṭ from aqsaṭa, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya questions its derivation; the author discusses comparative morphology.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: مم بني أفعلا التفضيل. أعني: أقسط. وأقوم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers deriving aqsaṭ from triliteral qasaṭa meaning “act justly,” avoiding the alleged morphological irregularity.
rows.anchor: والذي ينبغي أن يحمل عليه أقسط هو أن يكون مبنيا من قسط الثلاثي بمعنى عدل.

rows.speaker: ابن السيد عن ابن السكيت عن أبي عبيدة، ابن القطاع
rows.claim: Lexicographers report qasaṭa as both just and unjust, while aqsaṭa with hamza means only just, making aqsaṭ regular.
rows.anchor: حكى ابن السكيت في كتاب الأضداد عن أبي عبيدة: قسط جار، وقسط عدل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “More just with God” means more just under God's judgment because it prevents oppression.
rows.anchor: ومعنى: أقسط عند الله. أعدل في حكم الله أن لا يقع التظالم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “More reliable for testimony” means firmer and sounder; deriving aqwam from aqāma is irregular to some grammarians, while qāma avoids that issue.
rows.anchor: ومعنى: أقوم للشهادة، أثبت وأصح.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows aqwam to derive from aqāma under Sibawayh's approach or as a relational form from qawīm.
rows.anchor: وتقدم قول الزمخشري إنه جائز على مذهب سيبويه أن يكون من أقام، وقال أيضا: يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “for testimony” attaches to aqwam with object-like meaning; omitting it and using a direct accusative is restricted to poetry.
rows.anchor: ويتعلق: للشهادة، بأقوم، وهو من حيث المعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: السلمي، author
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī reads “that they do not doubt” with a masculine plural verb; the omitted comparison after “closer” is “than not writing.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: أن لا يرتابوا بالياء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence moves from obedience to God's just judgment, to reliable testimony, to eliminating doubt; writing and witnessing reassure the parties.
rows.anchor: ونسق هذه الأخبار في غاية الحسن، إذ بدىء أولا بالأشرف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubt may concern denial by the debtor, a witness forgetting, the testimony, amount or due date, or uncertainty for witness, judge, and parties.
rows.anchor:
قيل:
والمعنى: أن لا ترتابوا بمن عليه الحق أن ينكر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Present trade means either cash sale without a term or a movable-goods sale, usually small; al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk specify hand-to-hand exchange.
rows.anchor: في التجارة الحاضرة قولان: أحدهما: ما يعجل ولا يدخله أجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You circulate it among yourselves” means passing goods hand to hand or repeated trading, implying taking possession.
rows.anchor: وفي معنى الإدارة، قولان: أحدهما: يتناولونها من يد إلى يد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected because immediate sales are not deferred debts; writing may be omitted because it protects against uncertainty about amount, description, and term. Other views connect the exception to the debt or writing command.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستثناء في قوله: إلا أن تكون، منقطع لأن ما بيع لغير أجل

rows.speaker: عاصم، الباقون
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads “trade, present” in the accusative, with kāna incomplete; others use nominative and a complete verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم: تجارة حاضرة، بنصبهما على أن كان ناقصة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For most exegetes, “no blame” means no harm in omitting writing because writing is not obligatory; those who require it interpret the phrase as “no sin.”
rows.anchor: ونفي الجناح هنا معناه لا مضرة عليكم في ترك الكتابة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing all sales, immediate or deferred, is safer against disagreement; another interpretation limits the command to present trade.
rows.anchor: وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم هذا أمر بالإشهاد على التبايع مطلقا، ناجزا أو كالئا،

rows.speaker: الجحدري، الحسن، عبد الرحمن بن يزيد، الحكم
rows.claim: They say the witnessing command was abrogated by the permission to trust one another.
rows.anchor: قيل: وهذه الآية منسوخة بقوله: فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري، ابن عمر، الضحاك، ابن المسيب، جابر بن زيد، مجاهد، عطاء، إبراهيم، الشعبي، النخعي، داود بن علي
rows.claim: They hold witnessing obligatory; al-Ḍaḥḥāk requires it even for greens and ʿAṭāʾ for any price. Al-Ṭabarī says an unwitnessed sale defies God's Book.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي محكمة، والأمر في ذلك على الوجوب قال ذلك أبو موسى الأشعري،

rows.speaker: الحسن وجماعة، ابن العربي
rows.claim: They treat the command as recommendation and guidance, not compulsion; Ibn al-ʿArabī identifies this as the majority position.
rows.anchor: وذهب الحسن وجماعة إلى أن هذا الأمر على الندب والإرشاد لا على الحتم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An active reading forbids a writer altering the document or a witness concealing, changing, or withholding testimony; al-Zajjāj prefers this. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ also explain harm as refusing with excuses about being busy.
rows.anchor: واحتمل هذا الفعل أن يكون مبنيا للفاعل فيكون الكاتب والشهيد قد نهيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، طاووس، الضحاك، السدي
rows.claim: Under the passive reading, they say others must not harm the writer or witness by burdening them, disrupting their work, or making unreasonable demands.
rows.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون مبنيا للمفعول، فنهي أن يضارهما أحد بأن يعنتا،

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the passive reading, supported by ʿUmar's unassimilated reading: the opening addresses transaction parties, not writers and witnesses, and the warning fits parties forbidden to cause harm.
rows.anchor: واختاره الطبري لأن الخطاب من أول الآيات إنما هو للمكتوب له،

rows.speaker: عمر، ابن عباس، مجاهد، ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Their reading is reported with the first rāʾ unassimilated and either kasra or fatḥa; unassimilated pronunciation is Ḥijāzī and assimilation Tamīmī.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو عمرو عن عمر، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، وابن أبي إسحاق: أن الراء الأولى مكسورة،

rows.speaker: ابن القعقاع، عمرو بن عبيد، عكرمة، ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Their variants include a jussive rāʾ, an unassimilated verb with accusative kātiban, and a raised doubled rāʾ used as a negative form that strengthens the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن القعقاع، وعمرو بن عبيد: ولا يضار، بجزم الراء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the active reading, “if you do so” means causing harm; fusūq bikum means transgression attached to you or located within you, the latter more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وإن تفعلوا لمضارة أو الضرار فإنه، أي الضرار، فسوق بكم أي: ملتبس بكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning addresses writer and witness under an active reading, the parties under the passive reading, or everyone regarding all commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في: تفعلوا، عائد على الكاتب والشاهد، إذ كان قوله: ولا يضار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear God” means avoiding harm or observing all commands and prohibitions; it follows the warning of transgression.
rows.anchor: واتقوا الله أي: في ترك الضرار، أو: في جميع أوامره ونواهيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God teaches you” is an independent sentence reminding of the blessing of knowledge; taking it as circumstantial is very weak because imperfect circumstantial verbs ordinarily do not take this waw.
rows.anchor: ويعلمكم الله هذه جملة تذكر بنعم الله التي أشرفها: التعليم للعلوم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge encompasses all and signals recompense; repeating “God” makes three independent statements: command to piety, reminder of grace, and promise or threat.
rows.anchor: وأعيد لفظ الله في هذه الجمل الثلاث على طريق تعظيم الأمر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some ascetics invoke the verse to avoid legal sciences; Abū Ḥayyān objects that knowledge is needed to know piety.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا ما يتمثل بهذه بعض المتطوعة من الصوفية الذين يتجافون

rows.speaker: مجاهد، الضحاك
rows.claim: They infer that pledges and trust apply only in travel and reject pledges at home; the majority allow pledges at home and with a scribe. Travel represents an excuse, and the Prophet's armor pledged at home shows the condition is not restrictive.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب مجاهد، والضحاك: إلى أن الرهن والائتمان إنما هو في السفر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel represents any excuse that prevents writing or witnessing, including busy periods and nighttime.
rows.anchor: ونبه بالسفر على كل عذر، وقد يتعذر الكاتب في الحضر

rows.speaker: أبي، مجاهد، أبو العالية، ابن عباس، الضحاك
rows.claim: Some read kātiban as kutuban, a verbal noun or plural of writer; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take it as plural for multiple cases, and Abū al-ʿĀliya also reads kutuban as plural of kitāb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية: كتابا على أنه مصدر، أو جمع كاتب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ among farhān, ruhun, and ruhn; grammarians debate plural formation, Abū ʿAmr prefers the reduced dialect form, and Yūnus says rihān is Arabic but common for horses; al-Aʿshā's verse witnesses rahn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فرهان، جمع رهن نحو: كعب وكعاب.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء، الأعشى
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr says rihān is used for horses; al-Aʿshā's poem gives an example of rahn as the plural for pledges.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: لا أعرف الرهان إلا في الخيل لا غير،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Held in possession” requires taking; all accept possession by creditor or agent, while the majority accept a neutral custodian and ʿAṭāʾ, Qatāda, al-Ḥakam, and Ibn Abī Laylā do not.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من قوله: مقبوضة، اشتراط القبض. وأجمع الناس على صحة قبض المرتهن،

rows.speaker: الشافعي، أبو حنيفة، المالكية
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa make possession a condition of validity; Mālik makes the contract binding before delivery and compels transfer, possession being required for full benefit. All agree the pledge is incomplete without it.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر من الآية أنه لا يصح إلا بالقبض، وبه قال الشافعي وأبو حنيفة،

rows.speaker: مالك، أبو حنيفة، الشافعي
rows.claim: Mālik says return to the pledgor voids the pledge; Abū Ḥanīfa preserves it if returned as loan or deposit; al-Shāfiʿī voids it whenever returned.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في استمراره، فقال مالك: إذا رده بعارية أو غيرها بطل.

rows.speaker: الجمهور، المالكية
rows.claim: The majority require valuable, saleable, deliverable property and reject a debt as collateral and uncertain items; Mālik permits a debt and uncertain property such as runaway slave, stray camel, fetus, fish in water, or unripe fruit.
rows.anchor: فقال الجمهور: لا يجوز رهن ما في الذمة.

rows.speaker: مالك، الشافعي، أبو حنيفة، الحسن بن صالح
rows.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī permit an undivided share whether divisible or not; Abū Ḥanīfa rejects it altogether; al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ permits it only if indivisible.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في رهن المشاع، فقال مالك، والشافعي: يصح فيما يقسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “On a journey” means “while travelling”; wa-lam tajidū has several syntactic attachments, and farhān is predicate of an omitted subject: “the security is a pledge.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى: على سفر، أي: مسافرين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a creditor trusts the debtor and advances property without writing, witnesses, or pledge, the debtor must repay it without evasion or delay; jurists agree repayment is obligatory and enforceable.
rows.anchor: أي: إن وثق رب الدين بأمانة الغريم، فدفع إليه ماله بغير كتاب

rows.speaker: أبي، السجاوندي
rows.claim: Ubay reads fa-in ūmina in passive form, “if people trust him”; al-Sajāwandī reports fa-in iʾtamana as trust without a written instrument or pledge.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي: فإن أومن، رباعيا مبنيا للمفعول،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “his trust” may refer to creditor or debtor; amāna may mean the owed thing or act of trust, with “debt” understood elliptically.
rows.anchor: والضمير في: أمانته، يحتمل أن يعود إلى رب الدين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported readings alter the hamza of alladhī uʾtumina by vowel indication, ishām, or substitution with yāʾ; Abū Ḥayyān questions some notations and explains its original two hamzas.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن، وورش بإبدال الهمزة ياء، كما أبدلت في بئر

rows.speaker: عاصم، الزمخشري
rows.claim: A rare ʿĀṣim reading assimilates the tāʾ substituted for hamza; al-Zamakhsharī rejects it, though other grammarians report it as a poor dialect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في شاذه: اللذتمن، بإدغام التاء المبدلة من الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor must fear God's punishment in repaying entrusted property; “God, his Lord” stresses piety at acknowledgment and repayment, echoing 2:282.
rows.anchor: وليتق الله ربه أي عذاب الله في أداء ما ائتمنه رب المال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concealing testimony is forbidden where a right may be lost; Ibn ʿAbbās says testify when summoned and report directly to the person concerned, not merely to an official.
rows.anchor: ولا تكتموا الشهادة هذا نهي تحريم، ألا ترى إلى الوعيد لمن كتمها؟

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī reads the prohibition in third-person plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: ولا يكتموا، بالياء على الغيبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concealment means withholding testimony; sin is assigned to the heart because testimony is knowledge held there, using part for whole and emphasizing the heart as source of outward action; a prophetic hadith compares it to the body's governing morsel.
rows.anchor: ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه كتم الشهادة هو إخفاؤها بالامتناع من أدائها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority parse āthim as an active participle with qalbuhu its raised subject; al-Zamakhsharī offers a fronted predicate, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya's analysis is rejected by Basran grammarians except on Abū al-Ḥasan's approach.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور: آثم، اسم فاعل من: أثم قلبه، و: قلبه، مرفوع به

rows.speaker: ابن عطية، ابن أبي عبلة، مكي، الزمخشري
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests qalbuhu is partitive apposition; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads it accusative, parsed by Makkī as explanatory despite definiteness. Other parses compare it with object-like constructions or apposition to inna; a variant has athama qalbahu, “he made his heart sinful.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ قوم: قلبه، بالنصب، ونسبها ابن عطية إلى ابن أبي عبلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān identifies the first grammatical analysis as preferred.
rows.anchor: والإعراب الأول هو الوجه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge covers all acts, including concealment and proper delivery of testimony; it is a severe threat because knowledge entails recompense.
rows.anchor: وفي الجملة توعد شديد لكاتم الشهادة، لأن علمه بها يترتب عليه المجازاة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses contrasting paronomasia in debt/indebtedness, writer/writing, and entrustment/trust.
rows.anchor: التجنيس المغاير في قوله: إذا تداينتم بدين، وفي قوله: وليكتب بينكم كاتب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It uses matching paronomasia in “do not conceal testimony” and “whoever conceals it.”
rows.anchor: والتجنيس الممائل في قوله: ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repetition stresses following the right: “right” recurs, while ʿalā signals the creditor's position and claim.
rows.anchor: كرر الحق للدعاء إلى اتباعه، وأتى بلفظة على للإعلام أن لصاحب الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage pairs opposites in forgetting/reminding and small/large; it also uses comparison, specification, and repetition.
rows.anchor: والطباق في قوله: أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر، لأن الضلال هنا بمعنى النسيان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing catalogue identifies ellipsis and explains implied subjects and objects in writing, dictation, testimony, repayment, and not concealing testimony.
rows.anchor: والحذف في قوله: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، حذف متعلق الإيمان.
